claims.text: The initial alloy is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
The proposed intervention is pack aluminization with controlled Al vapor activity and an intermediate diffusion-barrier layer.
The proposed treatment is conducted at 1000–1050 °C for 1–2 hours in argon with controlled Al activity, followed by controlled cooling.
Modified pack aluminization will form a uniform, coherent, continuous, and adherent corundum Al2O3 scale on HfNbTaTiZr.
The intermediate diffusion barrier will limit excessive Al penetration into the alloy bulk.
The Al2O3 surface layer will act as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
The Al2O3 layer will significantly reduce oxygen ingress at high temperature.
Limiting Al ingress will preserve the underlying alloy microstructure.
Preserving the underlying microstructure by limiting Al ingress will preserve the alloy's mechanical properties.
The treatment will greatly improve oxidation resistance at 1000 °C relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The treated alloy will exhibit minimal oxidation weight gain at 1000 °C.
The protective scale will remain adherent during the proposed high-temperature exposure.
Room-temperature tensile ductility will remain essentially unchanged at 8–16% after treatment.
Yield strength at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹ will remain essentially unchanged at 163–530 MPa after treatment.
Departures from the specified temperature, exposure time, or atmosphere may destabilize the protective scale or cause excessive Al diffusion.
